hypothesis: Making the declared [64,96) readout phase physically real -- by routing every output-TARGETING synapse through a high-delay bank so no output can fire before tick 64 -- helps evolution find a better FastMultiHeadLUT->SPNet mapping than the ungated build, where outputs are driven straight through by the input volley and rank each other on spikes emitted before the network has computed anything.
design: Two arms, paired. Identical in every respect except the gate. Because seed_genome draws the base genome BEFORE apply_out_delay_gate touches it, the two arms at a given seed start from the SAME topology and the SAME weights, differing only in the delays of output-targeting synapses. 3 seeds per arm, 6 runs.

config._why_this_config: matches exp001_k32-baseline (K=32, batch 64, stdp_lr 0.01, d_max 20), the chapter's standard single-pool setup, so the gate is the only thing that differs from a run we already understand

metric: held-out Kendall tau-b, corrected by each model's own label-shuffle null, on the 2000 never-trained samples

meta_counts._note: the gate appends OUT_D_MAX - OUT_D_MIN + 1 = 17 metas; raising d_max to 80 instead would have cost 160
